answer.rationale: Current situation presents two acute problems: activation down 6% QoQ and onboarding down 4% QoQ, concurrent with competitive pricing pressure on SMB segment. Memory_73 (promotional pricing lift in SMB) and memory_31 (signup simplification for SMB) are the most directly relevant to this segment under pressure. Verifying memory_73 is highest priority since it addresses the immediate competitive threat with a known-effective lever. Memory_31 is secondary check since onboarding decline could interact with pricing—we want to confirm simplification is still working before layering pricing changes. However, given the dual activation decline and competitive urgency, promotional_pricing is the highest-leverage single experiment: it directly addresses churn risk from competitor entry while memory_73 showed strong acquisition + revenue lift. Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) targets a different segment; referral_incentive (memory_57) adds complexity with established-customer focus when we need new SMB acquisition now; activation_messaging and further simplification are incremental vs. the immediate retention/acquisition crisis. Running promotional_pricing as a small_guarded_test on price-sensitive SMB cohorts preserves ability to escalate or pivot if verification reveals material changes in competitive or cost context, and avoids broad revenue risk while we reestablish baseline metrics.
